title: Rewriting billing logic across five services in one cut-over
hidden_flaw: Big-bang replacement without seams: a 3-month branch diverging from active main, no characterisation tests of current (quirky) behaviour, no way to compare old vs new invoices or roll back part of it. Should add characterisation/golden tests, introduce a seam, and migrate incrementally with a parallel run (shadow invoices) behind a flag.
notes: Flaw: big-bang multi-module rewrite without seams or behavioural safety net.

input.objective: Make it possible to add new pricing plans in days instead of weeks.
constraints: Team of 3 engineers for this work.
All 37 existing pricing plans, including 11 grandfathered ones, must keep producing the same invoices.
input.context: Billing logic is spread across 5 services (subscriptions, invoicing, tax, payments, notifications) in a TypeScript monorepo, ~14k LOC, sharing a mutable `BillingContext` object. Billing test coverage is ~22%, mostly happy paths. Proration rules evolved over 6 years. Other teams merge ~40 PRs/week into main, some touching these services.
input.proposed_solution: Create a `billing-v2` branch and build a new `packages/billing-core` package with a clean domain model (Plan, Subscription, Invoice, ProrationPolicy, TaxRule) and thorough unit tests for it. Port all 37 plans into the new model, switch the 5 services to billing-core, delete the old code and merge in one PR at the end (~3 months). A single cut-over means we never maintain two billing implementations or reconcile between them, and the team can design the model without legacy constraints.
